title: Platform systems & services — how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, retrospective & roadmap (Q4 2026)
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview:
This document consolidates the platform engineering team’s canonical references for systems & services, onboarding how-tos, dashboards and alerting standards, runbooks for common incidents, a short retrospective of the prior quarter, and the Q4 2026 roadmap. It is intended to be the single entry point for engineers and SREs operating Redwood’s platform runtime and control plane.

Purpose & scope:
- Purpose: reduce time-to-resolution for incidents, standardize observability and onboarding, and make the roadmap and ownership explicit.
- Scope: all components owned by eng-platform and eng-serving-runtime teams: control plane services (api-gateway, routing, config-service), serving runtime (runtime-api, batch-scheduler, kvcache), telemetry (metrics-proxy, tracing-collector), and the platform console.

Team ownership & on-call (summary):
| Service | Primary owner | Pager | SLO (availability) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| api-gateway | Priya Shah | pager: #pager-api-gateway | 99.95% 
| runtime-api | Diego Ramirez | pager: #pager-runtime | 99.9% 
| batch-scheduler | Maya Chen | pager: #pager-scheduler | 99.5% 

Note: full on-call rotation and detailed contacts are maintained in the Team Wiki page linked below.

Systems inventory (high level):
- api-gateway: ingress, routing policies, rate limiting. Handles customer-facing requests for hosted API.
- control-plane-config: model catalog, rollout policies, customer config store (encrypted).
- runtime-api: inference runtime front-end (short requests; low-latency paths).
- batch-scheduler: long-running batch / heavy throughput jobs, autoscaling.
- kvcache: cached prefixes & KV cache service used across runtime nodes.
- metrics-proxy & tracing-collector: telemetry ingestion and forwarding to observability backend.

Service onboarding how-to (quick steps):
1. Create an ADR draft in confluence under eng-platform/decision-records describing the service goals, SLOs, failure modes, and scalability targets.
2. Create a repo skeleton following platform template (use cli: platform-kit init --service <name>).
3. Add service to infra repo with terraform modules for networking, autoscaling, IAM roles. Refer to infra-standards/networking checklist.
4. Add observability: 
   - metrics (Prometheus): implement the standardized metric families (request_total, request_duration_seconds, error_total, node_cpu_seconds).
   - tracing: instrument top-level RPCs with trace context. Make sure service emits span name: <service>.request.handler.
   - logs: structured JSON with keys {request_id, model_id, route, status, latency_ms}.
5. Add dashboard manifest: dashboards/<service>-overview.json and alert rules in alerts/<service>-alerts.yaml.
6. Run chaos tests (locally or in staging) against the service using the chaos harness: chaos-runner --playbook platform-service-failure.yaml.
7. Schedule a 30-45 minute onboarding review with eng-platform (owners + SRE) to review SLOs, runbooks and escalation.

Dashboards & alerting standards:
- Dashboard layout: Overview (top-level traffic & errors), Latency (P50/P95/P99 by route), Capacity (CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth), Recent traces (sampled), Error breakdown (5xx vs 4xx), Cost metrics (tokens/sec, tokens/cost).
- Naming convention: platform/<service>/overview and platform/<service>/detailed.
- Alerting guidance (rules below are baseline; product teams may tighten):
  - Sev 1 (pager): availability drop. Trigger when 5m rolling availability < 99% for any customer-facing route or if error rate > 5% for 5m. Pager to primary and eng-platform on-call.
  - Sev 2 (slack + email): latency regression. Trigger when P95 latency > 300ms for 10m for short/interactive routes or P95 > 2s for long/streaming routes.
  - Capacity (warning): node available capacity < 15% across a region for 10m.
  - Resource OOM: OOM kills > 3 across the fleet in 5m.
  - SLO burn: error budget burn rate > 8x projected for 1h.

SLO summary (canonical):
| Product SLO | Target | Measurement window | Error budget |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Customer-facing API availability | 99.95% | 30d | 0.05% |
| Short-request P95 latency | <200ms | 7d rolling | N/A (performance) |
| Embeddings batch throughput | 95th percentile >= configured baseline | 7d | N/A |

Runbooks (common incidents):
1) High P95 latency on runtime-api (interactive requests)
- Symptoms: P95 latency > 300ms, increased queue depths, traces show high scheduling wait.
- Immediate actions (0-10m):
  1. Check runtime-api overview dashboard and cluster autoscaler status.
  2. Run: kubectl get pods -n runtime | grep Pending or CrashLoopBackOff
  3. Check queue depth metric: metrics:runtime_api_queue_depth. If queue_depth > 2000, scale up worker pool: kubectl scale deploy/runtime-worker --replicas=<current+2>.
  4. If autoscaler not responding, restart controller: kubectl rollout restart deployment/cluster-autoscaler -n infra.
- Triage (10-60m):
  1. Identify slow nodes: metrics:node_cpu_seconds and GPU utilization. Evict noisy jobs (kubectl cordon/evict).
  2. Rollback recent deploy if latency spike coincides with a rollout: gcloud container clusters get-credentials ... && kubectl rollout undo deployment/runtime-api.
  3. If KV cache miss rate increased, revert any recent cache invalidation request.
- Post-incident: open an incident report, tag root cause, and run retrospective.

2) Model-serving OOMs / GPU OOMs
- Symptoms: OOMKill events, runtime container restarts, degraded throughput for specific model.
- Immediate actions:
  1. Identify the model and node: kubectl describe pod <pod> and check env MODEL_ID.
  2. Temporarily reduce max_sequence or batch size for that model via control-plane-config: PATCH /v1/configs/<model_id> {"max_batch": 16}.
  3. If problem persists, cordon node and schedule pod to other nodes: kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data.
  4. Notify ML infra and model-onboarding teams.
- Post-incident: generate a workload card for the model (memory profile, sequence distribution) and add a quantization/serve-profile recommendation.

3) Control-plane config-service outage
- Symptoms: control-plane errors for rollouts or failed reads/writes to configs.
- Immediate actions:
  1. Check config-service leader status (etcd/consul): curl http://config-service:2379/v2/keys/health.
  2. If leader unavailable, failover: run consul operator failover or promote backup leader per runbook.
  3. If data corruption suspected, restore from last verified snapshot (follow backup-restore runbook).

Retrospective highlights (last quarter):
- Incident summary: two Sev1 incidents: 1) region-wide autoscaler misconfiguration causing sustained 12m outage for dedicated customers; 2) unexpected OOMs after a model quantization rollout. Both incidents triggered improved processes below.
- Key lessons learned:
  - Add a pre-rollout autoscaler dry-run for changes to scaling policies.
  - Improve model rollout gates: require staging perf tests that include memory profiling and 95th percentile latency under representative load.
  - Increase telemetry retention for runtime traces from 7d -> 21d for regression triage.
- Action items (owner and ETA):
  1. Autoscaler dry-run CLI and CI check (owner: Maya Chen, ETA: 2026-03-15).
  2. Model rollout perf gate in onboarding (owner: Diego Ramirez, ETA: 2026-04-01).
  3. Increase trace retention in telemetry (owner: Observability team, ETA: 2026-02-28) — completed.

Q4 2026 roadmap (prioritized):
- Q4 milestone 1 (Nov–Dec): Platform runtime cost optimizations — intelligent batching improvements and kernel selection enhancements to reduce per-token GPU time by ~15%. (owner: eng-serving-runtime; success metric: 15% reduction in tokens/GPU-hour).
- Q4 milestone 2 (Dec–Jan): Dedicated autoscaling policy improvements and pre-rollout dry-run for commits to scaling configuration. (owner: eng-sre/eng-platform).
- Q4 milestone 3 (Jan–Feb): Platform console dashboard refresh — consolidate service-level views and add per-route SLO drilldowns. (owner: eng-platform; success metric: 95% coverage of active routes).
- Q4 milestone 4 (Jan–Mar): Runbook automation — auto-escalation playbooks for SLO-burn and automated mitigation for transient latency (e.g., temporary scaledown of low-priority workloads). (owner: eng-platform & automation team).

Team wiki & useful links:
- Platform team wiki (living): /eng-platform/team-wiki. Contains on-call roster, runbook templates, RFCs and onboarding checklist.
- Dashboards: grafana.platform.redwood.com (link to dashboard folder: platform/<service>).
- Alerts: alerts repo: git@github.com:redwood/platform-alerts.git (path alerts/).
- On-call: pager duty schedule: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/schedules.
- Incident process: /oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process.

Appendix A — escalation matrix (short):
1. Pager (sev1): primary on-call -> eng-platform lead -> eng-sre manager -> CTO on-call.
2. Sev2: slack to #platform-alerts -> on-call follows up next business hour.

Appendix B — change log (high level):

If you notice missing ownership or a new service that is not in the inventory, open a ticket: platform-team backlog -> label: onboarding-request and request a 1:1 onboarding review.
